summary: The pre-extinction fossil half is well supported by public data: the Harnik et al. 2012 genus-by-bin table (occurrences, grid-cell occupancy, extinct/survivor flag, lithology and environment covariates; CC0) and the Paleobiology Database API. Species-level, modern human-exterminated cases have no open trajectory dataset: IUCN needs a token and holds final assessments, and Neotoma coverage of extinct late Quaternary species was not confirmed.
next_step: Download the Harnik CSV (5.1 MB) and cross-check column names against the README; for the human-exterminated clause, compile a species list (e.g. from IUCN extinct species plus historical abundance series) as a separate small table.
obstacles_confirmed: Occurrence counts are abundance proxies; the Harnik table records genera, not species.
No open repository of pre-extinction abundance series for human-exterminated species was found.
IUCN API requires a token (HTTP 403 without).
